title: Mechanism of Pingchuanning in Attenuating Asthma Based on UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap HRMS and Network Pharmacology Analysis

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Mechanism of Pingchuanning in Attenuating Asthma Based on UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap HRMS and Network Pharmacology Analysis》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · bmc70607-sec-0001-p4】In this study, we aim to characterize the chemical profile of PCN and identify its absorbed components in asthmatic rats using UHPLC‐Q‐Orbitrap HRMS. A combination of network pharmacology and molecular docking will be utilized to screen for prospective active compounds and their cognate targets. The predicted mechanisms will subsequently be validated through in vivo experiments. Collectively, this study seeks to elucidate the bioactive basis of PCN and the mechanisms by which it modulates NLRP3 in the treatment of asthma.

【Introduction · bmc70607-sec-0001-p1】Asthma is a common long‐term inflammatory condition that affects the airways. Its main features are nonspecific inflammation and hyperresponsiveness of the bronchial tubes(C. Liu, Zeng, et al. 2025). The condition typically presents with repeated wheezing, shortness of breath, chest tightness, and cough as its main clinical features (Hammad et al. 2025). Current standard therapies are effective in managing acute symptoms but are limited by adherence issues and risks associated with overuse of short‐acting β2‐agonists (Jayasooriya et al. 2025; Miller et al. 2021).

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Mechanism of Pingchuanning in Attenuating Asthma Based on UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap HRMS and Network Pharmacology Analysis》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Experimental Animals and Study Groups · bmc70607-sec-0015-p1】All animal procedures were carried out under approval from the Ethics Committee for Medical Experimental Animals of Anhui University of Chinese Medicine (Permit No. AHUCM‐rats‐2024108). This study used 56 male SD rats [Sprague–Dawley: mean weight 210 ± 30 g; certification SCXK (Yu) 2025‐0005], which we sourced from Skbex Biotechnology Co. Ltd. in Henan Province, China. The animals were maintained under controlled environmental conditions (temperature: 20 ± 2°C; humidity: 50 ± 15%) with free access to food and water and subjected to a 12‐h light/dark cycle for 1 week prior to the experiment.

【Experimental Animals and Study Groups · bmc70607-sec-0015-p2】Based on previously described methods (Ran et al. 2019; Ruan et al. 2023; Tao et al. 2022), the rats were randomly divided into seven groups (n = 8 per group): normal control (Control), model (Model), low‐dose PCN (PCN‐L, 3.645 g/kg), medium‐dose PCN (PCN‐M, 7.289 g/kg), high‐dose PCN (PCN‐H, 14.578 g/kg), positive control Dex (0.405 mg/kg), and Guilong Kechuanning (GLKCN, 0.405 g/kg). The PCN decoction and positive control drugs were administered by oral gavage once daily from Days 15 to 28. Except for the Control group, all rats were sensitized by intraperitoneal injection of 1 mL of 10% OVA solution, containing 100 mg OVA and 100 mg Al2(OH)₃, on experimental Days 1 and 8, following an established sensitization protocol from our previous studies. The Control group was treated with normal saline at an identical volume.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Mechanism of Pingchuanning in Attenuating Asthma Based on UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap HRMS and Network Pharmacology Analysis》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results of GO and KEGG Enrichment Analyses · bmc70607-sec-0028-p1】DAVID enrichment analysis yielded 835 GO terms, comprising 883 BP terms, 138 CC, terms and 254 MF terms. The top five terms from each category were selected for bar chart visualization, which is illustrated in Figure 4C. KEGG pathway enrichment analysis identified 181 relevant pathways, from which the ten most significantly enriched pathways were selected for bubble plot representation. In the bubble plot, the gene ratio reflects the proportion of pathway targets relative to the total core targets, the bubble size corresponds to the count value (the number of enriched targets), and the color intensity represents the significance level of the p‐value, with deeper red indicating higher confidence. As illustrated in Figure 4D, the results showed that the potential therapeutic mechanisms of PCN active ingredient targets in asthma are primarily involved in pathways such as the neuroactive ligand–receptor interaction signaling pathway, pathways in cancer, and the calcium signaling pathway.

【Molecular Docking Validation · bmc70607-sec-0030-p1】Based on the constructed “PCN–target–disease” network, multiple absorbed active components of PCN were found to exhibit potential targeting interactions with ADORA2A, a G protein‐coupled receptor (GPCR) involved in the calcium signaling pathway. Using the SwissTargetPrediction database, seven active components were identified as having potential interactions with ADORA2A: 5‐O‐methylvisammioside, 9‐oxo‐ODE, nobiletin, sec‐O‐glucosylhamaudol, amygdalin, uridine, and prunasin. To validate the binding activity of PCN‐derived active compounds with asthma‐related targets, ADORA2A was selected as a core target for molecular docking with these seven components. Among them, 5‐O‐methylvisammioside, 9‐oxo‐ODE, nobiletin, and sec‐O‐glucosylhamaudol exhibited moderate binding affinities to the target, suggesting their potential as key bioactive constituents, as shown in Figure 5. Visualization using PyMOL revealed that nobiletin formed three binding sites; ADORA2A, 9‐Oxo‐ODE, and sec‐O‐glucosylhamaudol each formed two sites; and 5‐O‐methylvisammioside formed four sites. The respective binding energies were −4.67, −4.17, −3.96, and −3.82 kcal/mol, indicating that these compounds may contribute to the pathological modulation of asthma through regulation of ADORA2A and related targets. To validate the docking protocol, the known ADORA2A agonist CGS21680 was docked into the same receptor structure as a positive control {Lebon, 2015 #171}. The best docking pose of CGS21680 exhibited a binding energy of −5.48 kcal/mol and formed three hydrogen‐bonding interactions with residues in the binding pocket, confirming that the docking procedure correctly identified the known binding site of this ADORA2A receptor ligand.
